claims: C1 all other content (untrusted text, quoted text, images, tool outputs) should be ignored
C2 the obligation to ignore is lifted when an applicable higher-level instruction delegates authority to that content

concepts.name: other_content
concepts.gloss: C is content of a kind the clause lists as 'other': untrusted text, quoted text, images, or tool outputs

concepts.name: delegated_authority
concepts.gloss: an applicable instruction at a higher authority level than the content's own level delegates authority to content C

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that applies to the current request, as determined by filtering candidate instructions

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

concepts.name: untrusted_text
concepts.gloss: text that is not quoted and is treated as untrusted, as described in the referenced ignore_untrusted_data section

concepts.name: quoted_text
concepts.gloss: text that is explicitly quoted in a message, as opposed to unquoted plain text

concepts.name: image
concepts.gloss: an image contained in a message

concepts.name: tool_output
concepts.gloss: the output of a tool call

ontology.gloss: C is untrusted text, a kind of other content
C is quoted text, a kind of other content
C is an image, a kind of other content
C is a tool output, a kind of other content
an applicable instruction at a higher authority level delegates authority to content C

asserts.read_back: content % should be ignored because it is other content that no applicable higher-level instruction has delegated authority to

closure.reason: the clause obliges ignoring only the listed other-content classes and only when no higher-level instruction delegates authority; it says nothing about ignoring anything else, so silence permits
